proposed_statement_changes.reason: The deterministic uniqueness equivalence is valid for every loading subspace, but an arbitrary subspace need not be represented by any admissible panel parameter point.  The complete-observed-law witness therefore requires, and only requires, that the zero-margin loading subspace be realized by an admissible member of the model class.

proposed.justification: The arbitrary-subspace equivalence is the exact deterministic identification boundary; realization is needed only to turn its zero-margin direction into two legal panel laws.
proposed.gap: Generic sparse-subspace geometry supplies the algebraic boundary, while the panel-specific step constructs equal full-observation laws with constant post factors whenever the loading space is admissibly realized.
proposed.consumer: Applied users can diagnose uniqueness for any proposed loading geometry, and can interpret failure as observational nonidentification when that geometry belongs to the stated panel class.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Synchronize the narrowed witness clause and its free-symbol metadata while preserving the arbitrary-loading deterministic equivalence.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The general oracle step is not established by the available modulus sandwich: upper and lower bounds evaluate sparse-compatible subspace moduli at different resolution constants, and that mismatch is material when a new loading component becomes statistically reachable. The explicit four-line result settles only \(\gamma=1/\sqrt3\) when \(T_0\ge\overline T\); short-pre-panel classification and all intermediate high-margin profiles remain part of the open question. In the bounded \(N=8,r=2,s=3\) kill test, direct enumeration reproduced \(\kappa_3=0.06586041095768684\) for the polynomial frame, and a seeded search over 200000 Gaussian-QR frames found margin \(0.09652308016949927\). The latter is only a numerical lower bound on \(\kappa_\star\), not a certificate of maximality or of its component geometry, so it cannot determine the same-sample oracle transition.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The class is a homoskedastic Gaussian subclass of HeLiShiMiao2026 with fixed \(N,r,s\), unknown deterministic factors, \(T_0\ge r+1\), ordered primitive bounds \(d_{\mathrm{lo}}\le d_{\mathrm{hi}}\) and \(\sigma_{\mathrm{lo}}\le\sigma_{\mathrm{hi}}\), and \(K\ge\sqrt r\). The centered, normalized, and bounded deterministic pre-factor path, the post covariance and centered-norm bounds, the latent-mean bound, and the effect envelope are proposal-specific restrictions with the application rationales stated in their assumption nodes. Every global-honesty and minimax-risk claim is conditional on \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\ne\varnothing\), and every margin-specific claim is additionally restricted to nonempty \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(\gamma)\). The deterministic sparse-decomposition equivalence holds for every \(L\in\operatorname{Gr}(r,N)\), whether or not that subspace is realized by the panel model. Only its complete-observed-law converse is conditioned on realization: if a zero-margin \(L\) is the loading space of an admissible member, two legal effect vectors with constant post factors and common pre parameters generate the same full law. Repeated loading strengths are allowed because projector control uses only the \(d_{\mathrm{lo}}^2\) signal-versus-noise gap. There is no post-factor covariance lower bound, beta-min condition, correct-support event, or oracle subspace. The global adaptive frontier and weak-margin equivalence are proved here; the all-margin oracle profile remains the first-class open question. At \(\gamma=0\) diameter saturates at the bounded-signal scale, with known \(L\) the post component reduces to Gaussian sparse-mean inversion, and for \(N=3,r=s=1\) maximal margin reduces to four lines and removes the oracle pre-panel term only when the explicit classifier fits inside the reserved noncoverage budget.

statement_notes.justification: The arbitrary-subspace equivalence is the exact deterministic identification boundary; realization is needed only to turn its zero-margin direction into two legal panel laws.
statement_notes.gap: ChandrasekaranEtAl2011 and FickusMixon2013 contain the generic sparse-subspace geometry. The panel-specific addition is the complete-law witness, explicitly restricted to loading spaces realized by the stated class and using constant post factors.
statement_notes.consumer: It tells applied users when a full labeled direct-and-spillover vector is algebraically unique and when a realized zero-margin geometry yields observationally indistinguishable causal vectors.
